requirement: For each {term}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.hit` in a text or structural search, locate the start of the match in the outline of the **same snapshot**. Select the innermost item containing that position. The item's project-relative file path and selector form its `OutlineId`. When no smaller item contains the position, use the file root (empty selector).
rationale:
The tests cover every obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.enclosing_item`.

Both text and structural search produce hits through the one shared implementation, `crates/trust-but-verify/src/sources/hits.rs#impl[SourceProject<D>]/fn[find_hits]`. For each match it calls `file.at_offset(range.start)` and builds an `OutlineId` from the file path and that item's selector.

Obligations and the tests that check them:

- **Hit position in a single item, structural search.** `structural_tags_select_only_the_original_enclosing_item` runs a structural search and asserts the nodes `code.rs#fn[one]` and `code.rs#fn[two]` with their spans and text.
- **Same snapshot.** The same test rewrites the file after the search, and later reads and `finish_search` dependencies still resolve to the original `code.rs#fn[two]` fingerprint. `separated_hit_windows_preserve_the_function_declaration` also rewrites the file after the first iteration. Its second iteration still reports the original node and text.
- **Innermost item.** `separated_hit_windows_preserve_the_function_declaration` asserts the nested selector `runner.rs#impl[Runner]/fn[run]` for hits inside a method of an impl. That is the innermost item, not the enclosing `impl[Runner]`.
- **Path plus selector form the id.** Every test asserts the full `file#selector` node string.
- **File root when no smaller item contains the position.** `root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries` asserts `fragment.rs#` for sources with no outline items. `matches_crossing_item_boundaries_belong_to_the_item_at_the_start` asserts `pair.rs#` for a match starting in the whitespace between two functions.
- **Position is the start of the match.** `matches_crossing_item_boundaries_belong_to_the_item_at_the_start` has three cases. A match starting in the gap between items and ending inside `fn b` belongs to the root. A match starting on `}` of `fn a` and extending into `fn b` belongs to `fn[a]`. A match starting at `fn b` belongs to `fn[b]`.

The structural-search tests do not cover a nested item or a root hit. Both paths use the same `find_hits` code, so the text-search tests exercise that logic. I found no unacknowledged gap.

text: For each {term}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.hit` in a text or structural search, locate the start of the match in the outline of the **same snapshot**. Select the innermost item containing that position. The item's project-relative file path and selector form its `OutlineId`. When no smaller item contains the position, use the file root (empty selector).
A *source search hit* is one occurrence of a query in a retained file snapshot.
